original_value: There are several AD tools available that all implement different strategies for the reverse mode of AD. The most common strategies are primal value taping (implemented e.g. by ADOL-C) and Jacobian taping (implemented e.g. by Adept and dco/c++). Particulary for Jacobian taping, recent advances using expression templates make it very attractive for large scale software. However, the current implementations are either closed source or miss essential features and flexibility. Therefore, we present the new AD tool CoDiPack (Code Differentiation Package) in this paper. It is specifically designed for minimal memory consumption and optimal runtime, such that it can be used for the differentiation of large scale software. An essential part of the design of CoDiPack is the modular layout and the recursive data structures which not only allow the efficient implementation of the Jacobian taping approach but will also enable other approaches like the primal value taping or new research ideas. We will finally present the performance values of CoDiPack on a generic PDE example and on the SU2 code.

result.paraphrase: Several AD tools are available, each implementing different strategies for the reverse mode of AD. The most common approaches are primal value taping, as implemented for example by ADOL-C, and Jacobian taping, as implemented for example by Adept and dco/c++. Especially for Jacobian taping, recent advances based on expression templates make it highly attractive for large-scale software. However, existing implementations are either closed source or lack essential features and flexibility. We therefore introduce the new AD tool CoDiPack (Code Differentiation Package) in this paper. It is designed for minimal memory use and optimal runtime so it can be applied to the differentiation of large-scale software. A key aspect of CoDiPack’s design is its modular structure and recursive data structures, which not only support an efficient Jacobian taping implementation but also make other approaches such as primal value taping or new research ideas possible. Finally, we present CoDiPack’s performance results on a generic PDE example and on the SU2 code.
